cards.text: David, Israel's king, wrote this song for the choirmaster, and he opens with this: “I waited patiently for the LORD”. PATIENTLY. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and nobody in there would've used that word for me.

cards.question: David waited patiently for the LORD. Then the LORD inclined to him and heard his ___.

cards.text: And David wasn't waiting somewhere nice. He was down in the pit of despair, stuck in miry clay, the kind of mud that keeps your shoes as a souvenir.

cards.question: The LORD lifts David up out of that miry clay. Where does He set David's feet?
Even standing on that rock, David's footsteps are still slipping and sliding.

cards.text: So David's out of the mud with his feet on the rock, and his shoes are probably still down in the pit. Then the LORD puts something new in David's mouth.

cards.question: Fresh out of the pit, what does the LORD put in David's mouth?
David expects his rescue to stay a quiet secret between him and the LORD.

cards.text: Then David says it plainly: blessed is the man who has made the LORD his trust. Not the guy trusting his phone at 2 percent battery. THAT guy is about to have a very quiet afternoon.

cards.question: The blessed man David describes is the one who turns to the proud.

cards.text: Then David starts going through the wonders the LORD has done and the plans He has for us. And he says none can compare to Him.

cards.question: David wants to proclaim and declare the LORD's wonders and plans. What problem does he run into?

answers.text: There are more than he can count
No one in the crowd will listen
He can't find the right words

cards.text: Then David says something surprising: sacrifice and offering, burnt offerings and sin offerings, God did not desire them or require them. Wait. WHAT?

cards.question: Instead of sacrifice and offering, David tells God, “my ___ You have opened.”

cards.text: So David answers, “Here I am, I have come”. And he says it is written about him in the scroll.

cards.question: David shows up and says, “Here I am”. What does he say about doing God's will?

answers.text: He does it when he must
He fears he'll get it wrong

cards.text: David says God's law is within his heart. And centuries later, the book of Hebrews picks up these lines and says Christ spoke them when He came into the world (Hebrews 10:5–7).

cards.question: In the great assembly, the big gathering of God's people, what does David say he does?
David says he kept God's faithfulness and salvation hidden in his heart, away from the great assembly.

cards.text: Now the song turns, and David asks the LORD not to withhold His mercy from him. Kind of like telling the whole bakery how great my oven is, and then smelling smoke.

cards.question: David says God's loving devotion and faithfulness will guard him for a little while.

cards.text: Here's what's going on: evils without number surround David. Not a few. Not a bunch. WITHOUT. NUMBER.

cards.question: Evils surround David. What does he say his own sins have done?

answers.text: Overtaken him so he cannot see

cards.text: He says they're more than the hairs of his head, and his heart has failed within him. Friend, I walk around with THIS mustache. I know what a lot of hairs looks like.

cards.question: So David prays, “Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me; ___, O LORD, to help me.”

cards.text: Then David brings up the people who seek his life and wish him harm.

cards.question: What does David ask for the people who wish him harm?

answers.text: That they be ashamed and driven back
That he gets to strike them down
That they become his loyal friends

cards.text: Then there's the crowd saying to him, “Aha, aha!” Every group chat has one: the guy who replies with three laughing faces when you trip.

cards.question: David prays that those mockers saying “Aha, aha!” will be appalled at their own ___.

cards.text: Then David turns to a whole different crowd: everyone who seeks the LORD.

cards.question: What does David pray for all who seek the LORD?

answers.text: That they rejoice and be glad in Him
That they hide until danger passes

cards.question: David prays that those who love God's salvation will always say, “The LORD be magnified!”

cards.text: Then David ends with himself: “But I am poor and needy; may the Lord think of me.” Friend, I spent years forgotten in a drawer, so believe me, I know that prayer.

cards.question: David calls himself poor and needy. What does he call God?
David ends the psalm calm and relaxed, telling God to take all the time He needs.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 14 quotes "my ___ You have opened.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 17 has a dash outside a quotation: "David says God's law is within his heart. And centuries later, the book of Hebrews picks up these lines and says Christ spoke them when He came into the world (Hebrews 10:5–7)."

rule.text: No em dashes or en dashes to make a sentence longer.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 6 quotes "Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me; ___, O LORD, to help me.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish David's line ('He inclined to me and heard my ___'). It tests wording the baker hasn't seen. Card 1 also gives no sign yet that David is in trouble, so 'cry' can't be reasoned out over 'vow'.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Card 6 says the LORD puts 'something new' in David's mouth. That makes 'A new song' the only answer that fits and rules out the other two.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has three full sentences: the blessed-man line, the phone line and the 'THAT guy' line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'David starts going through the wonders' says he actually starts listing them. Verse 5 only says 'if I proclaim and declare them', so the 'if' is dropped.
'David wants to proclaim and declare' and 'What problem does he run into?' turn the text's 'if I proclaim and declare them' into a stated wish and an attempt that actually happened.

The blank asks the baker to fill in the exact word of the line ('my ___ You have opened'). Nothing on the earlier cards points to 'ears' over 'eyes' or 'lips', so this is a guess at wording, not at meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'So David answers' makes verse 7 a reply caused by verse 6. The text only says 'Then I said', and it leaves open how the two lines connect and who David is speaking to.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question uses card words to explain 'great assembly' as 'the big gathering of God's people'. It also adds 'God's people', which the text doesn't say.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The oven joke doesn't match the action. The comparison is something you bragged about failing on you. In verse 11, David asks for mercy because evils surround him, not because the God he praised failed. The comparison also suggests God's faithfulness was the thing that went up in smoke.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The story card has three full sentences: the hairs and heart line, the mustache line and the 'I know' line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
